text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The tax service is setting up an international computerised link-up with similar services abroad in order to hunt down tax-dodgers.
- The Duma has approved a law which makes top managers financially responsible for all the misfortunes of their enterprises.
- The giant Russian carrier Aeroflot will do its utmost to remain a state company, says the company's director general Valery Okulov.
- Telephone tariffs in Moscow will go up only gradually, says the network's director general Vladimir Lagutin.
- Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Bulgak says the government is mulling the idea of selling off its majority stake in Moscow's biggest exhibition ground VVC.
- The government has drawn up a list of depositaries and exchanges to work with Gazprom shares.
- The Central Bank will undertake all-out checks of commercial banks.
- Visa Int. has registered a Russian branch of its international Visa Association network.
SEVODNYA
- The Duma will investigate whether Russia's biggest insurer Rosgosstrakh was privatised in strict accordance with the law.
- Moscow city authorities are planning to do away with newly established France Telecom public phones which have proved extremely vulnerable to fake phone cards.
- The government is promising no financial aid to Russian food producers.
- Moscow has advised Russian regional authorities to issue bonds to pay their dues to the budget.
- Competition between state carrier Aeroflot and foreign companies is getting more and more acute.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The government has drawn up a plan to increase budget revenues by 34 trillion roubles ($6 billion).
- The government is urging regional authorities to issue bonds to cover debts incurred by local agricultural producers.
- Leasing foreign planes costs Russian companies millions of dollars while local plane makers have barely started an urgently needed reorganisation of their uncompetitive industry.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- The government is working overtime to get the new draft tax code voted by the Duma as soon as possible.
- The wealthiest 20 percent of Muscovites will start paying their rent in full from July 1, while others will continue to be subsidised by the municipality.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Russia's pharmaceuticals industry is in crisis and foreign producers are getting an ever-bigger share of the lucrative market.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
